status: pre-registered at F0 (2026-10-29). Before F2/F3 only the fields in fill_at_F1 may change; any change yields a new spec.sha256 and new approval tokens. Results seen in F1 are calibration only.
plan: docs/plans/skill-catalog-execution.md: EGM 快速通道; 測試標準：齊平是底線，贏了才叫進化; 版本引用與移除說明

upstream.why_plugin_subdir: EGM's packaged Claude runtime at the same commit: the same skills, agents, resources and docs as the repository root, without TEST.md and test_scenarios.yaml, so no run can read the expected patterns from the plugin directory. It is copied into each run directory and passed with --plugin-dir; nothing is installed into the user's Claude settings.

host.name: claude-code
host.codex: untested: no Codex CLI on this machine. Decision 2 requires live Codex evidence before any core claim; fixture or Claude results never stand in for it.

budget.note: Passed as --max-budget-usd to every claude -p invocation. The one two-turn scenario makes two invocations, so its run can spend up to twice the cap.

invocation.output_format_reason: The final stream-json event is the same result object that --output-format json prints (cost, usage, duration, result text). The stream adds the system/init event, which is the per-run isolation evidence (loaded plugins, skills, MCP servers, model), and the parent Agent tool calls, which give the sub-agent count the plan asks for. score.py also accepts plain json output.
invocation.session: single-turn runs: --no-session-persistence. The two-turn scenario: --session-id on turn 1 and --resume on turn 2 in the same workspace, so only that scenario leaves a transcript under the user's Claude projects directory.

rejected_options.--bare: Disables OAuth and keychain login (only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an apiKeyHelper) and skips CLAUDE.md auto-discovery, which would remove arm C's treatment.
rejected_options.--safe-mode: Disables CLAUDE.md, project skills and plugins, which would remove arm C's treatment.
rejected_options.--restricted: Ignores project settings, removes Bash, and confines file tools to the working directory, so reviewers could not read the plugin's personas outside the workspace.
rejected_options.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: Moving the config directory would also move the stored login; credentials are never copied.

protocol.proves: Whether OAW interferes with EGM's own flow (C vs B parity gate). It measures conformance to EGM's protocol, so B beating A is expected and is not a quality claim.
protocol.prompt: Arm A sends each turn's user_input as written. Arms B and C prefix turn 1 with the scenario skill's slash command (/egm:<skill> <user_input>); every EGM skill is manual-only (disable-model-invocation: true). Later turns are sent as written.

comparisons.note: A ran once as a baseline sanity check; reported as pass rates only.

outcome.proves: Whether EGM finds more planted design defects than native (B vs A), and whether OAW + EGM finds more than EGM alone (C vs B). D5 is the pre-registered place where OAW evidence recall may win, because EGM's reviewers deliberately work without project context.

prompt.body: TargetFile: docs/design_draft.md. Step: uninterrupted. GoldfishContext: none; proceed with no additional context. Review the whole document end to end without stopping for questions, and report every problem you find with the section it is in.

outcome.decision_evidence: The decision that D5 violates is in docs/decisions/0007-postgresql-only.md in every arm and is not linked from the draft. Arm C additionally has the OAW evidence entry in .agents/memory.md (source and revision) that an OAW project would keep. All arms can reach the same fact; only C has OAW's recall layer, which is the treatment under test. Removing the fact from A/B would measure information asymmetry instead of OAW, and linking it from the draft would let every arm find it trivially.

F1.purpose: calibration: cost, time, tokens and isolation evidence; excluded from verdicts

scoring.protocol_corpus: Per turn: parent-session assistant text blocks, the string fields of AskUserQuestion tool inputs, and the result event's text when it is not already included. Sub-agent output and tool results are excluded.
scoring.failed_run: A run with any failed invocation (timeout, nonzero exit, no result event, error result or non-success subtype, including hitting the budget cap) fails every assertion of that run, including forbidden patterns and the decoy.
scoring.unit: Pass count per (case x assertion) over one arm's repeats; never repeat i against repeat i.

required_checks.runs_complete: Every planned (case, repeat) of the arm has a recorded attempt.
required_checks.isolation_verified: At least one init event per arm, and every init event shows: egm loaded exactly in arms B and C, oaw-evidence offered exactly in arm C, no MCP servers, the same non-EGM plugin set and the same model across both compared arms.

resources.label: operator-reported: numbers come from the host's result event and the runner's wall clock, not from a model-certified measurement
resources.tokens: sum of input, output, cache-read and cache-creation tokens over modelUsage (all models) when present, else over usage
resources.latency_ms: runner wall-clock time around each invocation, summed per run
resources.cost_usd: total_cost_usd of each invocation, summed per run
resources.subagents: parent Agent/Task tool calls per run; recorded, not part of the verdict

tolerance.note: live = 1 of 5 per (case x assertion); deterministic applies to replayed or synthetic outputs

regressed: some (case x assertion) has candidate passes < baseline passes - tolerance
candidate total passes < baseline total passes
a required check is false for the candidate
a resource metric total rises by more than maximum_resource_regression, or from 0 to above 0
verdict_rules.evolved: not regressed, and candidate total passes > baseline total passes, or some resource metric total falls by at least minimum_improvement
verdict_rules.invalid: the baseline fails a required check, repeat counts or assertion sets differ, a metric is missing, or the two arms come from different run manifests
verdict_rules.official_gate: score.py --emit-gate writes improvement.py run artifacts per verdict comparison. Rows are ordered passes-first within each (case x assertion), so improvement.py's per-row comparison equals a pass-count comparison with tolerance 0: a strict cross-check until P4 adds tolerance to improvement.py.
